Calendar-aware rolling-origin evaluation

Source: R/evaluate.R
rolling_origin.Rd

Refits forecasting models at the end of every year and forecasts the following calendar year (monthly series), keeping track of the periods that contain the holiday and of the years in which the holiday moved to a different month than in the previous year ("moving years").

Usage

rolling_origin(y, dates, models, first = start(y)[1] + 8)

Arguments

y

Monthly `ts`.

dates

`Date` vector of the holiday used to flag periods.

models

Named list of functions `f(y_train, h)` that return point forecasts for the next `h` periods.

first

First test year.

Value

A data frame with columns `year`, `month`, `actual`, `model`, `pred`, `holiday` (the month contains the holiday) and `moving` (the holiday fell in a different month than in the previous year).

See also

[rolling_summary()]

Examples

# \donttest{
hol <- holiday_dates("idul_adha")
models <- list(
  classic_m6 = function(y, h)
    forecast(calvar_classic(y, hol, "stochastic", "stochastic"), h = h)$mean,
  snaive = function(y, h) forecast::snaive(y, h = h)$mean)
r <- rolling_origin(sapi, hol, models, first = 2023)
rolling_summary(r)
#>             all holiday other moving stable median_year
#> classic_m6 4.56    6.24  4.37   4.29   4.70        4.29
#> snaive     9.24   14.84  8.53  12.60   6.86        9.00
# }
